deductible.definition: The fixed amount you pay out of your own pocket before the insurer starts paying.
deductible.plain: Think of it as your share of the bill that comes first.
deductible.example: If your deductible is INR 5,000 and the covered bill is INR 50,000, the insurer pays from INR 45,000 onwards.

co-pay.definition: A percentage of the claim amount you agree to bear yourself at settlement time.
co-pay.plain: You always pay this percentage of the final bill; we pay the rest.
co-pay.example: With a 10% co-pay on a payable INR 50,000, you get INR 45,000 and bear INR 5,000.

copay.definition: Same as co-pay: a percentage of the claim amount you bear yourself.
copay.plain: You always pay this percentage of the final bill; we pay the rest.

sum insured.definition: The maximum total amount the insurer will pay in one policy year.
sum insured.plain: Your policy's overall ceiling for the year.
sum insured.example: A INR 5,00,000 sum insured means claims across the year cannot exceed that amount.

sub-limit.definition: A cap on a specific item inside your claim, such as room rent per day.
sub-limit.plain: Even if your overall cover is large, some line items have their own ceiling.
sub-limit.example: A 2% of sum insured room-rent sub-limit caps what is paid for the hospital room each day.

waiting period.definition: A period after the policy starts during which claims for specific conditions are not payable.
waiting period.plain: New policies need to run for a while before certain conditions are covered.
waiting period.example: A 30-day initial waiting period applies to most claims; a 2-4 year wait may apply to specified diseases.

pre-existing disease.definition: A medical condition you already had signs or symptoms of before buying the policy.
pre-existing disease.plain: Conditions diagnosed or treated before your policy began.
pre-existing disease.example: Diabetes identified before policy purchase is a pre-existing disease, usually covered only after a waiting period.

exclusion.definition: A condition, treatment or situation that the policy does not cover.
exclusion.plain: Situations your policy explicitly does not pay for.
exclusion.example: Cosmetic surgery without medical necessity is typically an exclusion.

cashless claim.definition: Treatment at a network hospital where the insurer pays the hospital directly.
cashless claim.plain: You do not settle the full bill yourself; we pay the hospital as per approval.
cashless claim.example: At a network hospital you show your card, get pre-authorization, and pay only your share.

reimbursement claim.definition: You pay the bills first, then claim the money back from the insurer.
reimbursement claim.plain: Pay now, claim later - keep all original bills.
reimbursement claim.example: At a non-network hospital you settle the bill, then upload invoices to get repaid.

pre-authorization.definition: The insurer's prior approval for treatment in a cashless claim.
pre-authorization.plain: The hospital asks us first, and we approve the treatment plan before you start.
pre-authorization.example: The hospital sends admission details; we approve the estimated amount within a few hours.

adjudication.definition: The process of applying policy terms to a claim to decide what is payable.
adjudication.plain: Where we check your claim against the rules of your policy and decide the amount.
adjudication.example: During adjudication we apply deductibles, co-pays, sub-limits and exclusions to the bill.

claim repudiation.definition: The formal rejection of a claim, with a written reason.
claim repudiation.plain: A formal 'no' with the reason in writing.
claim repudiation.example: A claim for an incident before the policy start date is usually repudiated.

grievance redressal.definition: The formal process to complain when you disagree with a claim decision.
grievance redressal.plain: The official escalation route if you think we got it wrong.
grievance redressal.example: File a grievance within 15 days of the decision letter; a reply is due within 15 days.

surveyor.definition: An independent expert who inspects the loss or damage for motor claims.
surveyor.plain: The person who comes to look at the damage and write a report.
surveyor.example: After an accident the surveyor inspects the vehicle and estimates repair cost.

idv.definition: Insured Declared Value - the current market value of your vehicle after depreciation, capped as the maximum motor claim payout.
idv.plain: What your vehicle is insured for, based on today's value minus depreciation.
idv.example: In a total loss or theft, settlement is limited to the IDV.

insured declared value.plain: What your vehicle is insured for, based on today's value minus depreciation.
insured declared value.example: In a total loss or theft, settlement is limited to the IDV.

third-party liability.definition: Cover for damage or injury you cause to other people or their property.
third-party liability.plain: Covers the other party, not you or your vehicle.
third-party liability.example: If you damage a shop front while driving, the shop owner's loss is settled under third-party liability.

own damage.definition: Cover for damage to your own vehicle from accident, theft, fire or natural calamities.
own damage.plain: Covers your own car or bike.
own damage.example: Flood damage to your own car is an own damage claim.

no-claim bonus.definition: A discount on renewal premium for every claim-free policy year.
no-claim bonus.plain: A reward for years when you did not claim.
no-claim bonus.example: Five claim-free years can earn up to a 50% discount on motor OD premium.

sla.definition: Service Level Agreement - the time the insurer commits to for a claims stage.
sla.plain: The clock we promise to work within.
sla.example: A 3-day SLA on under review means we aim to finish the review in three working days.

hospitalization.definition: Inpatient care where you are admitted for at least 24 hours.
hospitalization.plain: Being admitted to hospital, not just a visit.
hospitalization.example: Appendectomy with two nights stay is a hospitalization.

day-care procedure.definition: A listed treatment completed in under 24 hours without an overnight stay.
day-care procedure.plain: Treatments where you go home the same day.
day-care procedure.example: Cataract surgery or a colonoscopy are day-care procedures.

settlement.definition: The final payment made against an approved claim.
settlement.plain: The money we pay you after approval.
settlement.example: After deductions the settlement of INR 59,500 is credited to your account.

policy inception.definition: The date the policy cover officially begins.
policy inception.example: An incident on 10 September is not covered if your policy began on 14 September.
